fact_text: Dividend yield equals annual dividend per share divided by the share price, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Dividend Analysis (Concepts) | Part 04 | Stock Analysis & Market Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-02-21)

fact_text: Expected dividend growth equals expected annual dividend per share minus last annual dividend per share, divided by the last annual dividend, multiplied by 100.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Dividend Analysis (Concepts) | Part 04 | Stock Analysis & Market Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-02-21)

fact_text: Dividend cover equals earnings per share divided by dividend per share; in the analyst's illustration a company earning 10 lakh and paying out 2 lakh has cover of about 5 times.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Dividend Analysis (Concepts) | Part 04 | Stock Analysis & Market Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-02-21)

fact_text: Payout ratio equals dividend per share divided by earnings per share; in the analyst's illustration paying 2 of 10 lakh earned gives a payout of 20 percent.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Dividend Analysis (Concepts) | Part 04 | Stock Analysis & Market Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-02-21)

fact_text: The retained share of earnings is the part a company keeps for future expansion; in the analyst's illustration 8 lakh of 10 lakh earned is kept, the mirror of the 20 percent payout.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Dividend Analysis (Concepts) | Part 04 | Stock Analysis & Market Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-02-21)

fact_text: Expected payout ratio is the expected dividend per share divided by expected earnings per share, giving a forecast of the coming year's dividend.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Dividend Analysis (Concepts) | Part 04 | Stock Analysis & Market Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-02-21)

fact_text: Analysts forecast dividends differently: some assume the prior year's dividend repeats, while others model higher earnings or a decline if oil and gas reserves run down.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Company Dividend Analysis (Concepts) | Part 04 | Stock Analysis & Market Analysis' (YouTube, 2026-02-21)

fact_text: On the dividend tab, the latest dividend is the sum of the quarters declared within the fiscal year to date, while the last annual dividend is the full figure for the previous completed financial year.
